screens.name: Desktop global header (nav-belt)
screens.purpose: Persistent top bar on every page: brand/home link, delivery location, scoped search, account entry, orders, cart. The single most-used navigation surface on Amazon.
screens.layout: Desktop (>=1000px): one dark row (#131921, ~60px tall), left to right: [amazon logo + '.com' smile, links home] [pin icon + two-line 'Deliver to' block] [search bar flex-grow: 'All' department select | text input | orange magnifier button] [US flag + 'EN' caret] [two-line 'Hello, sign in / Account & Lists' caret] [two-line 'Returns / & Orders'] [cart icon with orange count + 'Cart']. Every item is a hit area with a 1px white outline + 2px radius on hover/focus. Below it, the sub-nav strip (separate screen). Header is NOT sticky on desktop; it scrolls away. Between ~1000px and 1250px the flag/language item hides first and the search bar shrinks. Below ~1000px on a desktop browser the layout squeezes (search goes min-width); on phones Amazon serves the separate mobile web header (see mobile screen).
elements: Logo: white 'amazon' wordmark with orange smile arrow and small '.com'; Prime members see 'prime' under the wordmark (memory)

Deliver-to block: location pin icon; signed-out line1 small grey 'Delivering to Seattle 98109' (IP-geolocated city + ZIP) / line2 bold white 'Update location'; older/alternate signed-out copy 'Hello' / 'Select your address'; signed-in line1 'Deliver to Mikey' / line2 bold 'Seattle 98109'

Search department select: grey (#e6e6e6) left segment with rounded left corners, label 'All' + caret; native <select> whose visible width auto-resizes to the selected label (e.g. 'Books', 'Electronics'); aria-label 'Select the department you want to search in'

Department options (in order, memory, list changes): All Departments, Alexa Skills, Amazon Autos, Amazon Devices, Amazon Global Store, Amazon Haul, Amazon One Medical, Amazon Pharmacy, Amazon Resale, Apps & Games, Arts, Crafts & Sewing, Audible Books & Originals, Automotive Parts & Accessories, AWS Courses, Baby, Beauty & Personal Care, Books, CDs & Vinyl, Cell Phones & Accessories, Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry, (indented) Women, Men, Girls, Boys, Baby, Collectibles & Fine Art, Computers, Credit and Payment Cards, Digital Music, Electronics, Garden & Outdoor, Gift Cards, Grocery & Gourmet Food, Handmade, Health, Household & Baby Care, Home & Business Services, Home & Kitchen, Industrial & Scientific, Just for Prime, Kindle Store, Luggage & Travel Gear, Luxury Stores, Magazine Subscriptions, Movies & TV, Musical Instruments, Office Products, Pet Supplies, Premium Beauty, Prime Video, Smart Home, Software, Sports & Outdoors, Subscribe & Save, Subscription Boxes, Tools & Home Improvement, Toys & Games, Under $10, Video Games, Whole Foods Market
Search input: white, placeholder 'Search Amazon', 15px text, no clear button; since May 2026 signed-in US users also get Alexa for Shopping prompts in the suggestion dropdown (search/press sources)
Search submit: #febd69 square button with dark magnifier icon, rounded right corners, hover #f3a847, input value 'Go' (aria-label 'Go')
Whole search bar gets a 3px orange (#f90) focus ring when input is focused
Language item: small US flag icon + 'EN' + caret (hover flyout, see Language flyout)
Account item: line1 small 'Hello, sign in' (signed-in: 'Hello, Mikey'), line2 bold 'Account & Lists' + caret
Orders item: line1 small 'Returns', line2 bold '& Orders'
Cart item: outline cart icon with count number in bold orange (#f08804) centered above the basket, bold 'Cart' label right of icon; count shows 0 when empty; caps display (large counts show '99+')

Hidden 'Skip to main content' link visible on first Tab focus; adjacent 'Keyboard shortcuts' popover listing Search (Alt + /), Cart (Shift + Alt + C), Home (Shift + Alt + H), Your orders (Shift + Alt + O), Show/Hide shortcuts (Shift + Alt + Z)
Signed-out first-visit tooltip: small white popover under Account & Lists with yellow 'Sign in' button and 'New customer? Start here.' link; appears after load and dismisses on outside click/scroll
states: Signed-out: 'Delivering to <City> <ZIP>' / 'Update location'; 'Hello, sign in'; cart count 0 (guest cart persists in cookie session)
Signed-in: 'Deliver to <FirstName>' / '<City> <ZIP>' from default address; 'Hello, <FirstName>'
Signed-in Prime: logo shows prime variant

Location unknown / non-US IP: 'Deliver to' / country name (e.g. 'Canada'), plus on first visit a popover 'We're showing you items that ship to Canada. To see items that ship to a different country, change your delivery address.' with 'Dismiss' and 'Change Address' buttons
Cart count 0 / 1-99 / '99+'; increments without reload after Add to Cart from PDP or add-to-cart side sheet
Search focused: orange ring, suggestion dropdown opens once a character is typed (signed-in with history: recent searches shown on focus with empty input)
Loading: header is server-rendered HTML, so it paints before JS; flyouts and suggestions only work after nav JS loads; before that, links navigate normally
Error: if suggestions call fails, dropdown simply does not appear; search still submits
interactions: Logo click -> home
Deliver to click -> opens 'Choose your location' modal
Department select change -> changes search scope (query param i=, e.g. i=stripbooks for Books); select width re-measures
Type in search -> autocomplete dropdown (see Search suggestions screen); Enter or button -> /s?k=<query>&i=<alias>&ref=nb_sb_noss (or nb_sb_ss_* when a suggestion was chosen)
Empty query + 'All' submit -> no navigation; empty query + a department selected -> goes to that department landing page
Language/flag hover -> language/currency flyout; click -> /customer-preferences/edit

Account & Lists hover (desktop) -> flyout opens after ~200ms intent delay and dims the page below the header with a translucent dark overlay; click -> Your Account (signed-in) or sign-in page (signed-out)
Returns & Orders click -> /gp/css/order-history; signed-out redirects to sign-in with return_to
Cart click -> /cart (gp/cart/view.html)
Alt+/ focuses search; Shift+Alt+C opens cart

screens.name: Choose your location modal
screens.purpose: Lets shoppers set delivery ZIP (signed-out) or pick a saved address (signed-in) so prices, availability and delivery dates on every page reflect their location.
screens.url_pattern: No URL change; modal over current page (AJAX glow endpoint). Triggered from header 'Deliver to' and PDP 'Deliver to' link
screens.layout: Centered modal ~375px wide, white body, header bar light grey (#f0f2f2) with bold title 'Choose your location' and close X at right. Body top: grey 13px explainer. Signed-out: full-width yellow 'Sign in to see your addresses' button; horizontal rule with centered 'or enter a US zip code'; row = ZIP text input (flex) + grey 'Apply' button; rule with centered 'or'; full-width dropdown 'Ship outside the US' listing countries; footer right-aligned yellow 'Done' button (appears when country chosen). Signed-in: vertical list of address cards (bold name, street, city/state ZIP, 'Default address' tag on default) with selected card outlined; link 'Add an address or pick-up point' and 'Manage address book'; then the same ZIP and country blocks. Mobile web: same content as a bottom sheet.
elements: Title 'Choose your location'
Explainer 'Delivery options and delivery speeds may vary for different locations'
Yellow button 'Sign in to see your addresses' (signed-out)
Divider text 'or enter a US zip code'
ZIP input (5 digits; accepts ZIP+4 in practice), prefilled with current ZIP
Secondary button 'Apply'
Divider text 'or'
Country dropdown 'Ship outside the US'
Yellow button 'Done'
Signed-in address cards with 'Default address' label
Link 'Manage address book'
Link 'Add an address or pick-up point'
Close X (aria-label 'Close')
states: Signed-out default: sign-in button + ZIP entry + country select
Signed-in with addresses: address cards first, current selection highlighted
Signed-in with no addresses: only 'Add an address or pick-up point' link + ZIP + country

Invalid ZIP (letters, fewer than 5 digits, non-existent ZIP): red inline message under input 'Please enter a valid US zip code' (message text corroborated by a Seller Central forum thread titled with it)
Applying: Apply button shows spinner/disabled
Success: modal shows 'Your location' confirmation briefly or closes; page reloads so header reads 'Delivering to <City> <ZIP>' and prices/dates update
International selection: 'Done' closes and header shows country name; products that do not ship are marked on PDP

Close: X, Escape, or click overlay (no change saved)
Enter key in ZIP input = Apply
Selecting an address card applies immediately and reloads

screens.name: Search suggestions dropdown (header autocomplete)
screens.purpose: Speeds query entry and funnels to high-converting queries; scoped suggestions push department filtering.
screens.layout: White panel attached flush under the search input, same width as input+button, max ~10 rows, 1px grey border, subtle shadow. Each row: magnifier or clock icon (recent) + suggestion text where the typed prefix is normal weight and the completion is bold. The top suggestion is sometimes followed by indented scoped rows 'in Electronics', 'in Cell Phones & Accessories'. Signed-in recent searches appear first with a purple/grey color and a right-aligned 'Remove' link. Since 2026 some rows are Alexa for Shopping prompts (question-style) that open the assistant rather than a SERP.
elements: Suggestion rows with bolded completion
Scoped department rows 'in <Department>'
Recent search rows with 'Remove' link (signed-in)
Alexa for Shopping question prompts (signed-in US, 2026)
states: Hidden when input empty (signed-out) / recent searches on focus (signed-in)
Typing: updates per keystroke, debounced
No suggestions: dropdown closes
Network error: silently absent
interactions: ArrowUp/ArrowDown moves highlight and writes suggestion into the input
Enter submits highlighted suggestion; Escape closes and restores typed text
Mouse hover highlights grey; click submits
Click 'Remove' deletes a recent search without submitting
Blur closes dropdown

screens.name: Account & Lists hover flyout
screens.purpose: Primary sign-in entry and hub for account destinations and lists without leaving the page.
screens.url_pattern: No URL; flyout anchored under 'Account & Lists'
screens.layout: White flyout ~500px wide, small caret pointing to the Account item, right-aligned to it; page behind dimmed. Signed-in top block: grey bar 'Who's shopping? Select a profile.' with 'Manage Profiles ›' (households with profiles). Then a 1px rule and two columns separated by a vertical rule: left 'Your Lists', right 'Your Account'. Signed-in right column ends with 'Switch Accounts' and 'Sign Out'.

'New customer? Start here.' - signed-out only

screens.name: 'All' hamburger side menu (hmenu) with drill-down
screens.purpose: Full catalog and program navigation in a left drawer; replaced the old 'Departments' dropdown after a 2019 A/B test (hamburger with sign-in call first and multi-level drill-down won).
screens.url_pattern: No URL; drawer over current page
screens.layout: Left drawer ~365px wide, full viewport height, white, own vertical scroll; rest of page covered by a dark translucent overlay (rgba(0,0,0,.8)) with a white X close button floating just right of the drawer's top edge. Drawer header: navy (#232f3e) bar with user-circle icon + bold 'Hello, sign in' (signed-out) or 'Hello, Mikey'. Body: sections separated by thick grey rules; each section has a bold 18px heading and 14px rows (~45px tall) with a right chevron '>' on rows that drill down. Sections in order: Trending; Digital Content & Devices; Shop by Department; Programs & Features; Help & Settings. Drill-down: the main list slides out left and a submenu slides in from right, headed by '< MAIN MENU' row (bold, with left arrow) then a bold department title and its links.

screens.name: Home page desktop (gateway)
screens.purpose: Landing page that merchandises categories, deals and personalized products; mostly a navigation hub into search/browse/PDP rather than a place to buy directly.
screens.layout: Page background light grey (#e3e6e6). 1) Hero carousel (id gw-desktop-herotator, confirmed in fetched HTML): full-bleed banner, max content width 1500px, image ~600px tall whose lower portion fades via gradient into the grey background. Tall transparent left/right arrow buttons at the edges (chevron icons, the whole side strip is clickable, 2px focus outline). No visible dots. 2) Card grid (gw-card-layout, confirmed): starts overlapping the hero (cards begin roughly 250-300px down the hero). 4 equal columns at >=1280px, 3 at ~1000-1280px, gap 20px, white cards, 20px padding, ~420px tall. Card title 21px bold dark (#0f1111) at top; content (single image or 2x2 quad of images with 12px captions); bottom link 13px teal (#007185, hover #c7511f underlined). First row usually includes the signed-out 'Sign in for the best experience' card in column 4. 3) After 1-2 rows of cards, full-width white 'shoveler' carousel rows (title left in 21px bold, optional 'See more' link beside it). Pattern continues: card row, carousel, carousel, card row, carousel... ~8-15 blocks total, some marked 'Sponsored'. 4) Bottom: horizontal rules around a centered signed-out prompt 'See personalized recommendations' + yellow 'Sign in' button + 'New customer? Start here.' Signed-in instead: 'Your browsing history' row. 5) 'Back to top' bar. 6) Footer.
elements: Hero slides (6-8): campaign images (e.g. Prime Video show, 'Shop deals', seasonal); each whole image is a link; prev/next buttons aria-labels 'Previous slide' / 'Next slide'

Quad card (2x2 with captions): e.g. 'Shop deals in Fashion' -> Jeans under $50 / Tops under $25 / Dresses under $30 / Shoes under $50, link 'See all deals'

screens.name: Mobile web shell and home (phone browsers)
screens.purpose: Phone version of the header/home served on amazon.com to mobile browsers; built around a full-width search and a single-column feed.
screens.url_pattern: / (same URL, mobile template chosen by user agent)
screens.layout: Header (not sticky; scrolls with page; an 'Open in the Amazon app' smart banner can appear above it): Row 1 on a dark navy-to-teal gradient: hamburger icon left, amazon smile logo, right side person icon + 'Sign in >' (signed-out) or '<Name> >' (signed-in), cart icon with count. Row 2: full-width rounded search field with placeholder 'Search Amazon' and a magnifier submit at right (no department dropdown). Row 3: horizontally scrollable text-link strip, no scrollbar (e.g. Prime, Video, Deals, Music, Books, Fresh, Registry, Gift Cards, Livestreams, Amazon Basics). Row 4: lighter teal bar with pin icon 'Deliver to <Name> - <City> <ZIP>' or 'Delivering to <City> <ZIP> - Update location' + down caret. Home body: signed-out top block 'Sign in for the best experience' with yellow 'Sign in' button and 'Create an account' link; then hero banner (swipe carousel with dots); then 2-column category tile grids inside white cards with titles; deal carousels with price, % off badge and 'Limited time deal'; best-seller carousels (swipe, show scroll snap); repeated. Bottom: 'Back to top' / 'Top of page' bar; compact footer with 2-column links (Your Amazon.com, Your Orders, Amazon Prime, Your Lists, Registry, Your Account, Customer Service, Sell, Browsing History, Your Recalls and Product Safety Alerts, Sign Out); locale row 'English' / 'United States'; 'Already a customer? Sign in' (signed-out); legal line + copyright. There is no persistent bottom tab bar on mobile web (that exists only in the native app: Home, You, Cart, Menu, and on newer builds a Rufus/Alexa entry).

flows.name: Signed-out first visit to home
steps: Open / -> header server-renders with 'Delivering to <IP city> <ZIP>' / 'Update location', 'Hello, sign in', cart 0
Sign-in tooltip pops under Account & Lists with yellow 'Sign in' and 'New customer? Start here.'
Hero carousel shows first slide and auto-advances; card grid overlaps the hero with 'Sign in for the best experience' card in column 4
User scrolls: best-seller carousels lazy-load; bottom shows 'See personalized recommendations' sign-in prompt, 'Back to top', footer

flows.name: Set delivery ZIP
steps: Click header 'Update location' / 'Deliver to'
Modal 'Choose your location' opens with focus in dialog
Type ZIP in input under 'or enter a US zip code', press Enter or 'Apply'
Invalid -> inline red 'Please enter a valid US zip code', stays open
Valid -> page reloads; header reads 'Delivering to <City> <ZIP>'; PDP delivery dates/prices now use that ZIP
Signed-in alternative: click a saved address card -> applies and reloads; header 'Deliver to <Name>' / '<City> <ZIP>'

flows.name: Scoped search from header
steps: Change 'All' select to 'Electronics' (select widens to fit)
Type 'wireless ear' -> suggestions: 'wireless earbuds', 'wireless earbuds in Electronics', ...
ArrowDown to highlight, Enter
Navigate to /s?k=wireless+earbuds&i=electronics; header keeps query text in input and 'Electronics' selected

flows.name: Browse via All menu
steps: Click 'All' in sub-nav -> drawer slides in, page dims
Under 'Shop by Department' click 'See all' -> list expands inline
Click 'Electronics >' -> panel slides to submenu with '< MAIN MENU' and 'Electronics' heading
Click 'Headphones' -> navigate to browse/search results for that node; drawer closes

flows.name: Sign in from home and return personalized
steps: Hover 'Account & Lists' -> flyout; click yellow 'Sign in' (or 'Sign in securely' card, or bottom 'Sign in')
/ap/signin with return_to=/ ; enter email -> Continue -> password -> Sign in
Redirect back to /: header shows 'Hello, <Name>', 'Deliver to <Name>' with default address ZIP, guest cart items merged into account cart (count updated)
Home replaces sign-in card with 'Pick up where you left off' / 'Keep shopping for'; bottom prompt replaced by 'Your browsing history'

flows.name: Home -> product -> back, history personalizes home
steps: Click product image in 'Best Sellers in Home & Kitchen' -> /dp/<ASIN>
Viewed ASIN recorded to browsing history (session or account)
Return to / -> 'Related to items you've viewed' and 'Inspired by your browsing history' rows now appear; sub-nav 'Browsing History' flyout (signed-in) lists the item

flows.name: Cart count stays in sync
steps: On PDP click 'Add to Cart'
Header cart count increments immediately (no page reload) and persists across pages
Click cart icon -> /cart

flows.name: Sign out
steps: Hover 'Account & Lists' -> click 'Sign Out' at bottom of 'Your Account' column
Land on sign-in page; header reverts to 'Hello, sign in'; cart count reverts to guest cart (usually 0)

flows.name: Mobile web navigation
steps: Tap hamburger -> left drawer 'Browse Amazon' with Trending / Top Departments
Tap overlay to close; tap 'Deliver to' bar -> bottom sheet ZIP entry -> 'Apply'
Tap search -> suggestions overlay -> submit -> results
Scroll to bottom -> 'Back to top'

flows.name: Keyboard-only shell navigation
steps: First Tab reveals 'Skip to main content'; Enter jumps past header
Alt+/ focuses search; Shift+Alt+C opens cart; Shift+Alt+Z shows shortcut list
Tab to 'All' + Enter opens drawer; Escape closes and returns focus

priorities.feature: Header: logo home link, search input + submit (Enter/button) to /s?k=
priorities.why: Search is the main entry point of the shopping loop; nothing works end to end without it.

priorities.feature: Header cart icon with live count (0, n, 99+) updating after add-to-cart without reload
priorities.why: Proves the loop visibly and is cheap (count read from cart state).

priorities.feature: Header account entry: 'Hello, sign in' vs 'Hello, <Name>' linking to sign-in or account, plus Sign Out
priorities.why: Needed to show auth state and reach sign-in before checkout.

priorities.feature: 'Returns & Orders' link to order history (sign-in gated)
priorities.why: Where the user confirms an order was placed; it's just a link to a page checkout already needs.

priorities.feature: Home page: category card grid (single + quad cards) linking to filtered search
priorities.why: Makes the home page a working browse hub instead of a dead end; static data, fast to build.

priorities.feature: Home page: 2-4 'Best Sellers in <Category>' product carousels linking to PDP
priorities.why: Direct path from home to product; reuses the product data and card component the search page already needs.

priorities.feature: Responsive mobile header (logo, account, cart row; full-width search row; deliver-to row)
priorities.why: Judges will check phone width; stacking one header is cheap, a broken mobile header costs heavily on UX score.

priorities.feature: Skip to main content link, visible focus rings, labelled icon buttons
priorities.why: Basic accessibility; a few lines of markup.

priorities.feature: Deliver-to header block + 'Choose your location' modal with ZIP validation ('Please enter a valid US zip code')
priorities.why: Iconic Amazon element and feeds PDP delivery estimates; ZIP kept in a cookie with a regex check is under an hour. Can use a native <dialog>.

priorities.feature: Search department 'All' dropdown (native select, ~20 departments we actually stock)
priorities.why: Native select costs almost nothing; only list departments with products so no scope returns empty results.

priorities.feature: Search autocomplete suggestions (prefix match on product titles/categories, keyboard nav, 'in <Department>' row)
priorities.why: Strongly expected on Amazon and makes search much faster; a simple API route plus an ARIA combobox.

priorities.feature: Account & Lists flyout (Sign in button, 'New customer? Start here.', short Your Account list)
priorities.why: Recognizable and cheap with CSS hover plus click/keyboard toggle; trim the links to pages that exist.

priorities.feature: Sub-nav strip with 'All', Today's Deals, Best Sellers, Customer Service
priorities.why: Static links; Today's Deals can point to a discounted-items search filter we already have.

priorities.feature: 'All' side drawer: Trending (Best Sellers, New Releases) + Shop by Department with one drill-down level and 'See all' expand
priorities.why: Main way to browse the catalog; one drawer component driven by the category tree.

priorities.feature: Hero banner (2-3 slides, manual arrows, pause, respects reduced motion)
priorities.why: Sets the Amazon look above the fold; a single static hero is the P0 fallback.

priorities.feature: 'Related to items you've viewed' / 'Pick up where you left off' from browsing history (guest via cookie/localStorage, account via DB)
priorities.why: Signature Amazon personalization; just a list of recently viewed product IDs, cheap and it makes the home page feel alive.

priorities.feature: Signed-out 'Sign in for the best experience' card and bottom 'See personalized recommendations' prompt; swapped for personalized cards when signed in
priorities.why: Shows the signed-out vs signed-in difference clearly with a conditional render.

priorities.feature: 'Back to top' bar + simplified footer (4 columns trimmed to real pages, legal line)
priorities.why: Static markup; completes the Amazon frame.

priorities.feature: Loading skeletons with fixed aspect ratios for hero, cards and carousels
priorities.why: Avoids layout shift, which is visible on Amazon; mostly CSS.

priorities.feature: Mobile left drawer and bottom-sheet location picker
priorities.why: Reuses the desktop drawer and modal with different CSS.

priorities.feature: Keyboard shortcuts (Alt+/ search, Shift+Alt+C cart) with shortcut help popover
priorities.why: Nice power-user touch, a few lines, but judges will rarely notice.

priorities.feature: Sub-nav 'Browsing History' hover flyout with thumbnails
priorities.why: Duplicates the home history row; build only if time allows.

priorities.feature: Page dimming overlay while header flyouts are open
priorities.why: Polish only.

priorities.feature: Deal cards with '% off' badge and 'Limited time deal' on home
priorities.why: Cheap if product data has listPrice, but not required for the loop.

priorities.feature: Signed-in address cards inside location modal
priorities.why: Needs the address book from checkout; ZIP entry covers the need.

priorities.feature: Recent searches with 'Remove' in suggestions
priorities.why: Requires per-user search log; low value in a demo.

priorities.feature: Language/currency/country flyout and translations
priorities.why: US English/USD only; a flag that does nothing is dead UI, so leave it out.

priorities.feature: 'Ship outside the US' country selector
priorities.why: No international shipping logic in scope.

priorities.feature: Digital Content & Devices menu (Prime Video, Music, Kindle, Echo, Fire TV, Appstore) and Programs & Features
priorities.why: Separate businesses with no catalog behind them; links would be dead ends.

priorities.feature: Registry, Gift Cards, Sell, Prime Video sub-nav links
priorities.why: Whole products of their own; no destination pages in 24h.

priorities.feature: Alexa for Shopping / Rufus prompts in search and AI overviews
priorities.why: LLM assistant is a separate project; it adds cost and latency and doesn't help the core loop. Revisit only if everything else ships.

priorities.feature: Household profiles ('Who's shopping?'), Switch Accounts
priorities.why: Multi-profile auth is out of scope.

priorities.feature: Sponsored ad cards/carousels and right-side promo slot
priorities.why: Ad inventory is Amazon's business, not the user's; removing it is an improvement.

priorities.feature: Footer sister-services grid (AbeBooks, IMDb, Woot!, Zappos, ...)
priorities.why: 27 outbound brand links, pure clutter for a rebuild.

priorities.feature: Prime logo variant and Prime flyouts
priorities.why: No membership system.

priorities.feature: First-visit sign-in tooltip auto-popover
priorities.why: Intrusive and repeats the account link and home sign-in card.

priorities.feature: Open-in-app smart banner on mobile
priorities.why: There is no app.

better_than_original: Sticky compact header on scroll (desktop and mobile): keep search and cart one tap away. Amazon's desktop and mobile web headers scroll away, so a shopper deep in a feed has to scroll back up to search.

Location update in place, no page reload: validate ZIP as you type (5 digits, inputmode=numeric), show the city it resolves to before Apply, update header and delivery estimates instantly. Amazon reloads the whole page.

Header flyouts that work by click, tap and keyboard, not hover only. Real buttons with aria-expanded, focus moved into the panel, Escape to close. No accidental hover-open that dims the whole page as the pointer crosses the header.

Department dropdown lists only departments we stock (about 15, not 60+), so a scope never returns an empty result. Use a fixed-width select so the search box does not jump in width when the scope changes.
Show price, rating and a short title on home carousel items. Amazon's 'Best Sellers in ...' rows are image-only, forcing a click just to learn the price.
Put Shop by Department first in the All drawer. Amazon leads with Trending and Digital Content (its own streaming/device businesses) before departments. Move focus correctly on drill-down and back.
Hero that respects prefers-reduced-motion, has a visible pause control and position dots, and no autoplay by default. Or a single static hero, which is less banner-blind and loads faster.

Much shorter home page: about 6-8 purposeful blocks (hero, 1-2 card rows, best sellers, deals, recently viewed) instead of 15+ rows including sponsored and near-duplicate 'inspired by / customers also viewed' rows.
No ads, no 'Sponsored' tiles, no promo slot in the sub-nav, no first-visit sign-in popover, no 27-brand sister-site footer grid. Footer trimmed to links that go somewhere.

No layout shift: fixed aspect-ratio boxes and skeletons for hero, cards and carousels, server-rendered first screen, lazy-loaded below-the-fold images with width/height. Aim for LCP under ~1.5s and CLS near 0; Amazon visibly pops content in on slower connections.
Recently viewed row with per-item remove and 'Clear history' inline, instead of a separate browsing-history page.
Guest personalization that survives sign-in: merge guest viewed items and guest cart into the account on sign-in and say so in a small toast ('We added 2 items from your guest cart').

Scroll-snap carousels with visible arrow buttons on focus as well as hover (Amazon's arrows appear only on hover, so keyboard and touch users cannot find them), plus aria-live 'Showing items 7-12 of 30'.
Consistent, accessible contrast and 44px touch targets on mobile. Amazon's mobile scroll strip and small grey header text are tight and low-contrast.
Theme-aware (light/dark) palette in the same navy/yellow/orange brand language. Amazon has no dark mode on web.
